samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` test names the list-before-delete ordering but never asserts it
samples.evidence: The case is titled "purges the documents it listed **before** the workspace was deleted" and its comment says "Listed first, because afterwards the server has nothing to list." The only assertion is `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith(["d1"], { dropArchives: true })`. `fetchDocuments` is a mock that answers identically whenever it is called, so moving `const doomed = await documentIdsIn(id)` to *after* `assertOk(res, ...)` in `workspaces.ts:97-103` leaves this test green. In production that reordering makes the listing run against a deleted workspace, `documentIdsIn` returns `[]`, and `purgeOfflineDocuments([])` is a silent no-op — the exact "silent no-op that read as a purge" failure the neighbouring comment (workspaces.test.ts:64-66) says this suite exists to catch, leaving full local copies of a deleted workspace's documents on disk until the 30-day sweep. No call-order assertion (`mock.invocationCallOrder`, a shared ordering array, or making `fetchDocuments` reject once the DELETE has fired) exists anywhere in the file.
searchedFor: grep for ordering arrays in workspaces.test.ts

samples.summary: No test asserts which `DurabilityLapse` is published; only the pure `tooltipFor` mapping is covered
samples.evidence: `sync-status-chip.test.tsx` exercises the lapse wording by calling `tooltipFor(...)` directly with a hand-written lapse value, so it proves the string table and nothing about which value is produced. The two producers are untested: `collab-document-provider.tsx:257-265` (the `unsupported`/`not-permitted`/`not-enabled`/`another-tab` chain — `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` has no lapse probe at all) and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:199-207` (`dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed`). `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx`'s only probe is `useDocumentDurability()` (line 97), never `useDurabilityLapse()`, and the sole `onWriteFailure` invocation passes `new Error('refused')` — the `err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'QuotaExceededError'` branch at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:151-156 that sets `out-of-space` is never entered. The design requirement quoted in sync-status-tooltip.ts ("Its tooltip must name which case applies") is therefore unverified end to end; a wrong or missing lapse ships as a tooltip naming the wrong cause.

samples.summary: `constructed` records the store options but no test ever asserts them — the runtime's store scoping is unverified
samples.evidence: `const constructed: Array<{ userId: string }> = []` (line 32) is pushed to by the `WafflebaseDocStore` mock (line 37) and reset in `beforeEach` (line 92), and `grep constructed` over the file returns only those three hits. Nothing asserts `constructed[0].userId === '42'` or that `isOpenElsewhere` was supplied. `OfflineRuntime` constructing its store under the wrong identity (or without the `whenUnknown: false`-scoped `isOpenElsewhere` it documents at offline-runtime.tsx:65-72) would pass this whole suite, while the sweep and reconcile would then run under a scope that is not the signed-in user's.

samples.summary: "installs the erase watcher" asserts only that the store argument is a function, not that it yields the store
samples.evidence: The case asserts `expect(typeof storeOf).toBe("function")` and never calls `storeOf()`. A regression that passed `() => undefined` — the precise shape the comment at offline-runtime.tsx:75-78 says must not happen ("Reads store and user at fire time, never captures them") — satisfies this assertion. Only the `userOf()` half is genuinely checked. The blast radius is limited because `watchForOfflineDisable` falls back to `new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` when the getter yields nothing, which is why this is minor rather than major.
searchedFor: read offline-runtime.test.tsx 'installs the erase watcher' case

samples.summary: `useNavigate` is mocked to a stable function, which mocks away the exact instability the navigateRef exists for
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('react-router-dom', () => ({ useNavigate: () => navigate }))` returns one constant `vi.fn()` for the life of the suite. The component's doc comment (offline-runtime.tsx:44-52) states the production reason for the ref: under a declarative `<BrowserRouter>` `useNavigate()` does *not* keep a stable identity, so listing it in the effect deps re-runs the whole housekeeping (new DB handle, another sweep, another archive listing, a title fetch per archive) on every in-app navigation. With the mock, adding `navigate` to the dependency array is invisible — no test can distinguish the ref from a direct dependency.

samples.summary: "subscribes from inside the DocumentProvider" uses the waiting pattern its sibling case documents as flaky
samples.evidence: This case does `await waitFor(() => expect(mounted.length).toBe(1)); expect(subscribers.length).toBe(1);`. The preceding case ("latches on the SDK's dropped-changes event") carries an explicit comment that waiting on `mounted` alone is wrong because `mounted` is pushed during render while the watch subscribes from an effect one level below, and that doing so "fires the event into an empty handler list often enough to fail roughly one run in five". The same race applies here, so this guard is nondeterministic — it can pass while the watch is mounted in the wrong place on a slower run, or fail spuriously. Waiting on `subscribers.length` (as the sibling does) would make it deterministic.
searchedFor: read collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx 'telling the store which removals are losses' describe

samples.summary: The traversal guard was weakened from "every request carries the encoded id" to "some request does"
samples.evidence: The loop was replaced by `expect(paths.some((pathname) => pathname.includes(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)))).toBe(true)`. The per-URL `not.toContain('/auth/logout')` still catches a raw `../../auth/logout`, so the traversal property mostly survives — but the encoding property is now satisfied by a single request. A route that stopped interpolating the id into one of several requests, or that interpolated it somewhere the `pathname` check does not look (a query string), is no longer distinguished from one that never carried it. The stated motivation (a companion `fetchDocuments()` request with no id) could have been met by exempting id-free URLs rather than by relaxing to `some`.

samples.summary: No test that a failing local purge cannot turn an accepted delete into a reported failure
samples.evidence: `deleteDocument` comments the purge as "Best effort, and never able to turn an accepted deletion into a reported failure" (documents.ts:161-164) and `deleteWorkspace`'s test comments "Local cleanup must never be able to fail the operation itself". In every test `purgeOfflineDocuments` is a bare `vi.fn()` or `mockResolvedValue(undefined)`, so the rejection path is never driven. `purgeOfflineDocuments` constructs `new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` *outside* its own try block (offline-erase.ts), so a constructor throw does reject — and `deleteDocument` awaits it before the success toast, and `deleteWorkspace` awaits it after `assertOk`. A `mockRejectedValue` case on each would pin the documented property.

samples.summary: Every durable-path test mocks `@yorkie-js/react`, so the `clientKey`/`store` props are only ever asserted against a mock that accepts anything
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` and `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` both replace `YorkieProvider` with a prop recorder, and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:40-47` explicitly casts the provider because the pinned types "predate" the `clientKey` alias. The repo pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22` (packages/frontend/package.json:66) while `MinClientKeyVersion` is `0.7.23`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and nothing exercises the real provider — every test forces the gate open with `vi.spyOn(capabilities, 'supportsClientKey')` or `vi.stubGlobal('__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__', ...)`. The consequence is that the prop spelling, and whether the SDK actually attaches the store under that key, are unverified by construction: a mis-named prop passes every test and surfaces only as a silently non-persisting feature once the pin is bumped.
searchedFor: read both durable test files' @yorkie-js/react mocks

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser` — the cross-account guard on orphan-snapshot collection — has no test
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters with `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1206), parsing `wb:{userId}:` out of the key. The only orphan case in the suite (`wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts`, "is collected rather than living forever out of reach") uses the key `doc-a`, which contains no `wb:` segment, so the regex never matches and the guard's true branch is never taken. A key such as `pk/wb:user-2:sheet-9/sheet-9` with its header removed — one account sweeping another account's orphan — is untested in both directions (wrongly collected, or wrongly spared forever).

samples.summary: `dropAllForUser({ keepArchives })` and `dropArchivesWhere(..., onlyUser)` have no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `grep keepArchives|onlyUser` over packages/frontend returns only the declaration sites: `offline-erase.ts:29` forwards the option but `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` and `watchForOfflineDisable` both call `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` with no options, and `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` parameter is never passed (`collectStale` omits it, `dropAllForUser` narrows via the range instead). Both are documented at length as protecting archives on an involuntary expiry, so the behaviour they describe is neither reachable nor pinned.
searchedFor: read offline-erase.ts eraseOfflineDataOnLogout / retryPendingOfflineErase call sites

samples.summary: The note recovery branch does not assert the archive is dropped, nor kept when the write fails
samples.evidence: "rebuilds a note as markdown written straight into a new note" asserts `created[0]`, `applied` empty, and the seeded text, but never `expect(await listRecoverableWork(store)).toEqual([])` — the drop-after-write ordering that the sheet branch pins in "forgets the archive only after the content is written" and "keeps the archive when writing the content fails". `recoverOfflineCopy`'s note arm has its own `await writeNote(...)` / `await store.dropArchive(work.id)` pair (offline-copy-recovery.ts:194-199), so the ordering property is asserted for one arm and assumed for the other.

finding.summary: `deleteWorkspace` test names the list-before-delete ordering but never asserts it

The only assertion is `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith(["d1"], { dropArchives: true })`. `fetchDocuments` is a mock that answers identically whenever it is called, so moving `const doomed = await documentIdsIn(id)` to *after* `assertOk(res, ...)` in `workspaces.ts:97-103` leaves this test green. verdict.reason: Verified independently: workspaces.test.ts:50-68 names the list-before-delete ordering in its title and comment but asserts only mockPurge's arguments. mockFetch (52-56) answers the GET and the DELETE (same /workspaces/team URL) identically and mockDocuments (57-60) is a fixed mockResolvedValue, so relocating `const doomed = await documentIdsIn(id)` (workspaces.ts:127) to after `assertOk` (workspaces.ts:131) keeps this test — and all three siblings at 70-107 — green. I searched repo-wide for a counterexample: `deleteWorkspace` appears only in workspaces.ts, workspaces.test.ts, url.test.ts (segment-encoding only, and its comment at 165-169 explicitly ignores the listing request's position), and workspace-settings.test.tsx:32 where it is an uncalled vi.fn(). `dropArchives` and `fetchDocuments` greps surface no other covering test; offline-erase.test.ts, offline-runtime.test.tsx and the backend workspace specs do not assert this. Ordering assertions do exist elsewhere in the codebase (documents.test.ts:73-83, tests/api/auth.test.ts:168-178), so the pattern is available and simply absent here. In lane (missing test for a documented, load-bearing behavior) and major: the untested regression is a silent purge no-op leaving full local copies of a deleted workspace's documents on disk.

finding.summary: The provider's new identity query (`['me','optional']` + `fetchMeOptional` + `initialData` seeding) is never exercised — every suite mocks `@tanstack/react-query` wholesale
finding.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx:185-192` adds `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, initialData: () => queryClient.getQueryData(['me']) })`. Both suites that render this component stub the whole library: `src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` (`vi.mock('@tanstack/react-query', () => ({ useQuery: () => ({data: undefined, isPending:false}), useQueryClient: () => ({getQueryData: () => undefined}) }))`) and `src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` (`useQuery: () => me`). Neither mock looks at `queryKey`, `queryFn` or `initialData`, so the queryFn is never called. The doc comment itself says using `fetchMe` here would send every anonymous `/shared/:token` visitor through `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm (logout + hard redirect to `/login`), and that the `['me']` seeding is what prevents a blank editor frame on private routes — a swap back to `fetchMe`, a changed key, or a dropped `initialData` would break a user path with no failing test. Searched: grep `fetchMeOptional`, `initialData|queryKey` across packages/frontend; only non-collab callers have their own coverage.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is real: collab-document-provider.tsx:184-192 configures useQuery with queryKey ['me','optional'], queryFn fetchMeOptional, retry:false and initialData seeded from queryClient.getQueryData(['me']). Both dedicated suites mock @tanstack/react-query wholesale (collab-document-provider.test.tsx:32-37; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:95-98), so the real query config is never evaluated — the durable suite's identity case (line 328) drives its own `me` object through the mock and covers only the pending-gate, not which function/key is used or the seeding. I searched wider than the reviewer: every test file naming CollabDocumentProvider (tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx, tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx, tests/app/documents/document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx, src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-document-durability.test.tsx, src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx). Three of these do supply a real QueryClientProvider — so the reviewer's "every suite stubs the library" phrasing is imprecise — but with the offline preference off, mayPersist is false and no assertion in them depends on the identity result (pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx:87-93 asserts only initialRoot; document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:39-47 aliases fetchMeOptional to the same mock as fetchMe, so a swap back would not fail it); shared-document-durability.test.tsx:24-31 mocks the provider module away entirely. `initialData` occurs exactly once in packages/frontend (the source line), and ["me","optional"] occurs only in source files. No frontend e2e suite exists and no test intercepts /auth/me. So the gap is genuine and in-lane: a swap to fetchMe (anonymous share visitors logged out and hard-redirected to /login), a changed key, or a dropped initialData (blank editor frame on private routes) would ship with every suite green — a user-visible path with no failing test.

finding.summary: No test that `removeMember` purges nothing when the server refuses the removal, although the parallel case exists for `deleteWorkspace`
finding.evidence: `workspaces.test.ts` has `deleteWorkspace` › "purges nothing when the server refuses the delete" (lines 92-107) but the `removeMember` describe (lines 110-145) only covers the success path and the cross-account guard. `removeMember` computes `doomed` before the request and purges with `{ dropArchives: true }` after `assertOk`; if that ordering regressed (purge moved before `assertOk`, or `assertOk` dropped), this user's local copies AND their archives — the only copy of work the SDK could not reconcile — would be deleted for a removal the server rejected, and nothing in the suite would fail. Searched workspaces.test.ts in full and grepped for `removeMember` elsewhere in packages/frontend tests.

verdict.reason: Verified the gap directly. `removeMember` (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:155-168) computes `doomed` before the DELETE, gates on `await assertOk(res, "Failed to remove member")` (:165), then purges with `{ dropArchives: true }` (:167). The `removeMember` describe (workspaces.test.ts:110-145) contains only two tests — the success purge and the cross-account guard — and both stub `mockFetch` exclusively with `ok: true` responses, so neither would fail if `assertOk` were dropped or the purge hoisted above it. The parallel guard IS tested for `deleteWorkspace` at workspaces.test.ts:90-107 (`rejects.toThrow()` + `expect(mockPurge).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`), confirming the asymmetry. I searched well beyond the reviewer's scope for a counterexample and found none: url.test.ts:101 calls the real `removeMember` but its beforeEach (:80) resolves every fetch as ok and it only asserts single-segment URL pinning; workspace-settings.test.tsx:28-40 mocks the whole `@/api/workspaces` module so the real purge logic never executes; offline-erase.test.ts:525 mentions `removeMember` only in a comment; a repo-wide grep for `purgeOfflineDocuments|dropArchives` in packages/frontend returns only 7 files, of which the sole purge-exercising tests are documents.test.ts (document deletion) and workspaces.test.ts. Backend workspace.service.spec.ts:303-381 tests the server refusing the removal, not the frontend's response to that refusal. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a regression in the assertOk/purge ordering would silently delete this user's local copies and their archives for a removal the server rejected, with no test failing.
